newsitem.title: USA: Oklahoma bombing trial will not be delayed.
newsitem.headline: Oklahoma bombing trial will not be delayed.

text.p: The attorney for Oklahoma City bombing defendant Timothy McVeigh said Tuesday he has not asked for a delay and the trial will begin as scheduled later this month.

"So this trial will start on March 31 with a selection of a jury. That's what our client wants. That's what we want and I think that's what everybody wants," Stephen Jones told reporters after leaving a closed door meeting with the bombing case judge and prosecutors.
"We did not ask for a continuance," Jones said. "We were all on the same page. We were surprised there was such unanimity of opinion among us."

Jones said Monday he might have to seek a delay in the trial because of a report published in the Dallas Morning News that quoted a defense document that purported to contain a confession from McVeigh.

Patrick Ryan, the U.S. attorney from Oklahoma City, told reporters he expected a fair jury to be selected. "I share the confidence of Jones and the court that the people here will be able to give Mr. McVeigh a fair trial," he said.
McVeigh has pleaded innocent to the April 19, 1995 bombing of the Alfred P. Murrah federal building in Oklahoma City, in which 168 people were killed and 500 injured.
